To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of digital tools in academia is still limited to a few areas and is mostly used by scholars who work in the humanities and social sciences and are employed at universities.
digital scholarship is an umbrella term that encompasses a variety of new scholarly practices that are not only supported by digital technologies but are also enabled by them.

the majority of the scholars we surveyed (a) have a positive attitude towards digital technologies, (b) use the web in the course of their work, and (c) are aware of the benefits and limitations of web-based tools for their research and teaching.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions:  What is digital scholarship and how is it changing the way we produce knowledge in academia?
how the digital transformation of scholarly communication and research is changing the ways in which we do research, teach and learn, and how we disseminate and evaluate our findings.
how the use of digital technologies in scholarly work has affected the way we think about knowledge, how we produce and disseminate it.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the web has changed the way we work.
digital scholarship is not a new concept, but rather the concept of digital scholarship is new, and the concept is evolving and changing.
there is no one single definition of digital scholarship.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been trying to find out what the new digital practices of scholars look like and what the implications are of these practices for the academic community.
we have developed a framework for a digital scholarship that is based on a critical reflection on current practices and that aims to support a more open and collaborative research culture.
we have been working on the development of a new approach to the study of scholarly communication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
digital scholarship is a reality and that the academy needs to embrace it.
the use of digital technologies in academia has been increasing over the years, and the use of social media has been increasing in particular.
the digital is not just a new tool for scholars, but it is a new medium for scholarship.
